The numerator is the product:
\[
\prod_{k=1}^{19} \left(1 + \frac{17}{k}\right)
\]
Each term \(1 + \frac{17}{k}\) can be rewritten as \(\frac{k + 17}{k}\). Therefore, the numerator becomes:
\[
\prod_{k=1}^{19} \frac{k + 17}{k} = \frac{(18 \cdot 19 \cdot \ldots \cdot 36)}{1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 19}
\]

The denominator is the product:
\[
\prod_{k=1}^{17} \left(1 + \frac{19}{k}\right)
\]
Similarly, each term \(1 + \frac{19}{k}\) can be rewritten as \(\frac{k + 19}{k}\). Therefore, the denominator becomes:
\[
\prod_{k=1}^{17} \frac{k + 19}{k} = \frac{(20 \cdot 21 \cdot \ldots \cdot 36)}{1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 17}
\]

We now form the ratio of the numerator to the denominator:
\[
\frac{\frac{18 \cdot 19 \cdot \ldots \cdot 36}{1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 19}}{\frac{20 \cdot 21 \cdot \ldots \cdot 36}{1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 17}}
\]

Simplifying this ratio, we notice that the terms from 20 to 36 in the numerator and denominator cancel out. The remaining terms are:
\[
\frac{18 \cdot 19 \cdot (1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 17)}{(1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 19) \cdot (20 \cdot 21 \cdot \ldots \cdot 36)}
\]

Recognizing that \(1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 19 = (1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 17) \cdot 18 \cdot 19\), we can further simplify:
\[
\frac{18 \cdot 19 \cdot (1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 17)}{(1 \cdot 2 \cdot \ldots \cdot 17) \cdot 18 \cdot 19} = \frac{18 \cdot 19}{18 \cdot 19} = 1
\]

Thus, the value of the given expression is:
\[
\boxed{1}
\]
